solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Youth flipping old man's fish

indicators.note: flipping turns the possessive for the old man over, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: old man is a familiar word for father, PA, so old man's is PA'S
the ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: A young man turns over his father's fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' reverses the possessive PA'S; 'Youth' is a young tree here, not a young person in the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapling is a young tree, and by extension a young person, a stripling.

clue.text: Film very masculine poet hugging Keith

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

indicators.note: hugging says the poet's name wraps around Keith

parts.note: T. S. Eliot, the poet
Keith is taken as written

explanation.surface: A film shows a very manly poet embracing someone named Keith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugging' splits the poet T. S. Eliot's surname after its third letter to hold Keith.
explanation.definitionFit: Some Like It Hot is Billy Wilder's 1959 comedy starring Marilyn Monroe, Jack Lemmon and Tony Curtis.

clue.text: Animal chart regularly hung from post

indicators.note: hung from says, in this down entry, the picked letters hang below the post

parts.note: a pole is a post

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of chart, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An animal chart is hung up on a post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' gives CAT from cHaRt. In a down clue the second piece hangs beneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a dark-furred mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Children with unlimited pieces of thin paper

indicators.note: unlimited means the word loses its limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: tissues are pieces of thin paper

explanation.surface: Children come with an endless supply of paper hankies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' strips T and S from TISSUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal or legal word for a person's offspring, as in 'died without issue'.

clue.text: Revolutionary drug too new: one deserves another

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests overturning things, so these letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A groundbreaking drug, too novel, is a favour to be repaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' rearranges DRUG TOO into GOODTUR. The definition plays on the saying 'one good turn deserves another'.
explanation.definitionFit: A good turn is a kindly favour; the proverb says one good turn deserves another.

clue.text: Each one stuffed with something baked

indicators.note: stuffed with says the word for one has the baked item packed inside it

parts.note: an ace is the card counting as one
a pie is baked in the oven

explanation.surface: Each portion is filled with a pastry dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is not I or A here but the playing card that counts as one; 'stuffed with' fills it with the baked dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece is an adverb meaning for every single one, the same as each in prices like two pounds each.

clue.text: Drink pop finally being promoted in Levantine city

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink

indicators.note: in this down entry the final letter of pop is promoted, raised to the front

explanation.surface: A drink and soda finally rising in a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally being promoted' moves the last P of POP to the top, giving PPO.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleppo is a major city in Syria, in the Levant on the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Unyielding island site clan reconfigured

indicators.note: reconfigured says the letters of site and clan are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An island's site is reorganised by a stubborn clan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconfigured' turns SITE and CLAN into NELASTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic means not stretchy, rigid, and so figuratively unwilling to bend or give way.

clue.text: Shorten most of drape length

indicators.note: most of means the word for drape loses its final letter

parts.note: a drape is a curtain

explanation.surface: Cut down most of a curtain's length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last N from CURTAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to cut short or reduce, a synonym of shorten.

clue.text: Trumpeter at front of pitch for key event

indicators.note: at front of places the trumpeter's name before the word for pitch

parts.note: Miles Davis, the jazz trumpeter
tone is the pitch or quality of a sound

explanation.surface: A trumpet player at the front of the field marks a key moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpeter' is Miles Davis, known by his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A milestone, literally a roadside distance marker, is figuratively a significant stage or turning point.

clue.text: Attention Lowry perhaps gives noblemen

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
the painter L. S. Lowry, given by his initials

explanation.surface: Listening to the painter Lowry brings in aristocrats.
explanation.walkthrough: L. S. Lowry was a British painter of northern industrial scenes; 'perhaps' marks his initials as one example of LS.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking below a marquess, so earls are noblemen.

clue.text: Chop pies and carve small game on screen

indicators.note: chop means cut up, so these letters are diced and rearranged

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to cut up pies and slice small pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop' rearranges PIES AND CARVE into SPACEINVADER; 'carve' is fodder, not a second signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Space Invaders is the 1978 arcade video game in which rows of aliens descend the screen.

clue.text: Catholic overcome by enticement to see something filthy?

indicators.note: overcome by says the abbreviation for Catholic is engulfed by the word for enticement

parts.note: a lure is a bait or enticement

explanation.surface: A Catholic yields to temptation and goes to see something dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'filthy lucre', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Money is proverbially called filthy lucre, so the cash itself is that dirty thing.

clue.text: Kingpin's best headgear shorn of diamonds

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

indicators.note: shorn of says the card-suit letter is cut away from the headgear

parts.note: a bandana is a scarf tied round the head
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: The gang boss has the finest headscarf, minus its jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shorn of' removes D (diamonds) from BANDANA, leaving BANANA. 'Kingpin's' is read as 'Kingpin is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is slang for the leading person, the boss of an organisation.

clue.text: Indicator of quality cooked meat eaten by Captain

indicators.note: eaten by says the stirred-up meat goes inside the captain's name

parts.note: Captain Kirk of Star Trek

indicators.note: cooked says the letters of meat are prepared into a new order

explanation.surface: The captain swallows some cooked meat that carries a quality stamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns MEAT into TEMA, which 'eaten by' puts inside KIRK after KI. The Kitemark is the British Standards Institution's safety and quality symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kitemark is a British certification symbol showing a product meets official standards.

clue.text: Superior maybe in need of a light

definitions.text: maybe in need of a light
definitions.meaning: read as ..., lacking a match, so perhaps needing a light

explanation.surface: Something better might still want lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: Matchless means unequalled, and match-less literally means short of a match for lighting.

clue.text: PM extracting British from engagement with Spain

indicators.note: extracting says the letter for British is pulled out of the fight

parts.note: a battle is a military engagement
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A prime minister pulls Britain out of a war with Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee was the British Labour Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led Britain as Prime Minister after the Second World War, so he is a PM.

clue.text: Noisy bird singer skinned well

parts.note: Joe Cocker, the English rock singer

indicators.note: skinned means well loses its outer letters, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A noisy bird sings well after being plucked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinned' leaves EL from wELl. Joe Cocker was an English rock singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockerel is a young rooster, famous for crowing loudly at dawn.

clue.text: Encourage characters bringing together zinc items

indicators.note: the answer's letters are characters spanning the join of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Some letters urge you to combine zinc objects.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or urge someone on, which is a strong way to encourage.

clue.text: Comfort 10 often found on this?

definitions.meaning: a games ..., the machine on which Space Invaders is often played

explanation.surface: Is comfort often found on this?
explanation.walkthrough: '10' refers to the answer to 10-down, SPACE INVADERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Console means soothe someone in distress, and a console is also a video-game machine.

clue.text: Record vehicle by empty Italian residence

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: empty means the inside of Italian is cleared out, keeping only its two end letters

explanation.surface: A record of a taxi beside a hollow Italian home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves IN, the outside letters of Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A log cabin is a simple house made of tree trunks, a type of dwelling.

clue.text: Exclude spirit that's consumed a good deal

parts.note: to bar is to exclude

indicators.note: that's consumed says the spirit has swallowed the letter a

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Banning a spirit that has been drunk a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's consumed' means the spirit has swallowed the A; 'a good deal' is not 'a lot' but the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is a purchase at a good price, which is what a good deal means.

clue.text: 18 classic elevated part of Vietnam capital

indicators.note: elevated says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A classic game rises from a part of the Vietnamese capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition omitted '18': it is 'console classic', '18' being CONSOLE, else '18' has no job. 'elevated' reads the hidden NAMCAP upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pac-Man is the 1980 maze game, a staple of arcade and home games machines.

clue.text: Feeling support for Hugo's character

parts.note: a hunch is an intuitive feeling
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A feeling of support for a figure created by Victor Hugo.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Hugo wrote The Hunchback of Notre-Dame, whose title character is Quasimodo.
explanation.definitionFit: Quasimodo, the bell-ringer in Victor Hugo's novel, is known as the Hunchback of Notre-Dame.

clue.text: Grub from back of cooker covered in hot stuff

indicators.note: covered in says that letter is wrapped by the molten rock

parts.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of cooker

explanation.surface: Food taken from the rear of the stove, smothered in something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grub' looks like food in the surface but means an insect larva. 'back of' gives R, and 'covered in' puts it inside LAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the soft larva of an insect, especially a beetle.

clue.text: Tips of pink tulips beneath meadow sprang up

indicators.note: beneath says, in this down entry, the picked letters sit under the meadow

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word

indicators.note: tips of picks the first letter of each of the two flower words

explanation.surface: Pink tulips' tips sprang up below a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips of' gives PT, placed under LEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapt is the past tense of leap, to jump, so it means sprang up.

clue.text: European left over figure of speech

indicators.note: over says the combined pieces are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A European departed, leaving only a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns EPORT into the answer. 'left' looks like a verb, departed, but it is port, a ship's left side.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figurative or metaphorical use of a word or expression.

clue.text: Mother and boy splitting horse fare for Paddington?

indicators.note: splitting says the mother and boy go between the letters of the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
ma is an informal word for mother
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A mother and son divide a horse, as food for a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington Bear, from Michael Bond's children's books, famously loves marmalade sandwiches; the question mark marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear's favourite food is marmalade, kept in a sandwich under his hat.

clue.text: Not initiating a serious crime makes sense

indicators.note: not initiating means the word loses its starting letter

parts.note: treason, betraying one's country, is a grave crime

explanation.surface: Avoiding a grave offence is the sensible course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initiating' drops the T that starts TREASON.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is the faculty of thinking sensibly, so sense and reason are synonyms, as in 'see reason'.

clue.text: Some Americans sink money into Asian country

indicators.note: sink as in investing, with into, says the money goes inside the country
into completes the instruction to place money within the country's name

parts.note: Laos is a country in South-East Asia
tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: Investors put cash into a South-East Asian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink ... into' places the money inside the country; tin is old British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Latinos are people of Latin American origin, so they are some of the population of the Americas.
